name: develop
summary: Develop a ticket or task with explicit choices for selection, verification, acceptance, merge and partial work. The first option at each point is the hands-off default.

options.label: A ticket
options.summary: Resolve a ticket through the configured ticket command.
options.change: In develop.declaration.json, set workflow.input.fields to { "ticket": { "type": "ticket" } }. In develop.ts use ticketInput(request) from develop/report.ts to pass the resolved ticket text to the turn.

options.label: A task text
options.summary: Develop the submitted prompt without a ticket lookup.
options.change: In develop.declaration.json, set workflow.input.fields to { "prompt": { "type": "string" } }. In develop.ts replace ticketInput with promptInput in the import and call. promptInput(request) passes the submitted text without a ticket lookup.

points.question: Who selects the next ticket or task?

options.label: The queue
options.summary: Select a ready ticket through the configured next-ticket command.
options.change: In develop.declaration.json, set workflow.queue to true ("queue": true).

options.label: A person
options.summary: A person submits the ticket or task when starting a run.
options.change: In develop.declaration.json, remove the workflow.queue field.

points.question: How should the tests be verified before review?

options.label: No additional verification
options.summary: Keep the current development, review and merge checks.
options.change: Leave develop/round.ts and the declaration unchanged for verification.

options.label: Red and green test check
options.summary: Verify an assertion failure on the base and passing tests on the pull request head before review.
options.change: In develop/round.ts import verifyRedGreen from develop/red-green.ts. In deliverPull, before acceptWork, call verifyRedGreen({ cycleId: pull.target, head: pull.commit, round }). Return a blocked outcome immediately; for non-null feedback return { merged: false, reason: verification.reason, output: verification.output }, so that developRound passes it to recover for the next fix turn. In develop.declaration.json add the command capability to workflow.capabilities and "commands": ["red-green"] to workflow, and command: ["run:red-green"] to methods. Add 6 to workflow.effectLimit. Configure the operator red-green command and checks.redGreen.

options.label: Greptile at 5/5
options.summary: Open or update the pull request and wait for Greptile to accept its commit at 5/5.
options.change: In develop/accept.ts call reviewByAgent({ subject, reviewer: { kind: "greptile" } }). develop/round.ts opens or updates the pull request first and passes its immutable commit and target as subject. Declare github wait-review.

options.label: A person
options.summary: Wait for a person's approval of the immutable commit. Denial with feedback requests another bounded turn.
options.change: In develop/accept.ts replace the import and call with reviewByPerson({ subject }). Remove reviewer and github wait-review from the declaration. develop/local.ts already uses reviewByPerson with the clean full commit from the worker report and the run target.

options.label: A review turn
options.summary: Run the review profile and require its explicit accept verdict.
options.change: In develop/accept.ts call reviewByAgent({ subject, reviewer: { kind: "turn", profile: "review" } }). For local merge replace reviewByPerson in develop/local.ts with that same call and its import. Declare claude run-turn:review and configure the review profile. Remove github wait-review from the declaration.

options.label: A panel of review turns
options.summary: Run two or three review turns with the profiles review-claude, review-codex and review-gemini, each with its own harness. A synthesizer turn with the profile review-synthesis combines their reports, drops the findings that the current change already fixes, and gives the verdict. A change verdict starts a fix round with the synthesized findings.
options.change: In develop/round.ts replace the acceptWork import with import { reviewPanel } from "./panel.ts". Pass state and report from developRound to deliverPull, and add state: DevelopState and report: DevelopReport to its request; import the type DevelopReport from develop/report.ts. In deliverPull replace the acceptWork call with reviewPanel({ state: request.state, report: request.report, pull: pull, reviewers: ["review-claude", "review-codex", "review-gemini"] }) and return a blocked outcome at once: if ("kind" in review) return review. For two reviewers remove one name from reviewers. Remove github wait-review from the declaration, add claude run-turn:review-claude, run-turn:review-codex, run-turn:review-gemini and run-turn:review-synthesis, and set workflow.effectLimit to 99. Configure the four profiles.

options.label: Cloving after the checks
options.summary: Open or update a pull request and merge after acceptance, the beforeMerge check and CI. Pass result.output into a fix turn on failure.
options.change: Call mergeWhenGreen({ pull, check: "beforeMerge" }) after acceptance. Use the pull returned by opening the pull request. Give the result.output to the next fix turn.

options.label: A person approves Cloving's merge
options.summary: Open or update a pull request, wait for merge approval, then run the beforeMerge check and CI before merging.
options.change: In develop/round.ts replace the mergeWhenGreen import and call with mergeByPerson({ pull, check: "beforeMerge", round }). Use the pull returned by openPull. repair passes the result.output unchanged to the next fix turn.

options.label: A person merges the local branch
options.summary: Leave the accepted branch for a person to merge by hand. Do not push or open a pull request.
options.change: In develop.ts import localRound as developRound from develop/local.ts. Remove the develop/pull.ts import, the preparePull call around the input (keep its argument as the input), the start labelTicket call and its check, the blockTicket call and endingRound. The local round reviews the worker report commit, then returns the local branch outcome. Declare only claude capabilities and run-turn methods; include run-turn:review when selected. Do not push or open a pull request.

points.question: What happens when the work is partial?

options.label: Return the ticket to the queue
options.summary: After merging partial work, record the remaining work and set cloving: ready for the first two partial runs. Set cloving: blocked from the third. Stop a run after three fix rounds.
options.change: After a merged result, call protectedEffect with capability: "github", method: "partial-issue", and a payload containing owner, repository, number, pullRequest and remaining. Use an explicit scope with phase, operation and round. The GitHub worker records the partial run and applies ready or blocked.

options.label: A person decides
options.summary: Ask what to do with partial work. Use the answer as feedback for a bounded continuation, or stop and leave it for the person.
options.change: For a pull-request workflow, in develop/round.ts import partialChoice from develop/partial-choice.ts. Immediately after the line that returns a blocked outcome of developReport, call partialChoice({ input, round, report }) and return any non-null result. develop/local.ts already does this. The helper calls waitForDecision({ gateId: partialGateId, kind: "question", prompt: partialQuestion }); an explicit answer feeds the next bounded turn and an empty answer stops.

points.question: What happens when a run cannot finish by itself?

options.label: Ask a person
options.summary: Try a short git or GitHub failure of open-pr, merge or label again after 60, 300 and 900 seconds, without a new turn, then stop blocked with the reason and the pull request link. Give the second merge conflict a conflict prompt. At the round limit, after the third conflict, or after a review without findings, ask a person for two more rounds, a stop with the pull request open, or a close of the pull request.
options.change: Keep export const recovery = "person" as "person" | "stop" in develop/recovery.ts. Keep github close-pr in the declaration methods. The default workflow.effectLimit of 87 covers six rounds with all retries.

options.label: Stop as today
options.summary: Fail the run on a failed GitHub effect, and stop blocked at the round limit without a question.
options.change: In develop/recovery.ts set export const recovery = "stop" as "person" | "stop". The retry, conflict and decision helpers then return the earlier results unchanged.

points.question: Do the workers keep a lessons file in the repository?

options.label: A lessons file in the repository
options.summary: Each development turn prompt includes .cloving/lessons.md, up to 16 KB. A missing file is the same as an empty file. Before its last commit, a turn can add up to three new lessons, each on one line in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English with the date and the ticket. The turn does not add a lesson that the file already has in the same or a similar form. When the file is larger than 16 KB, the turn joins similar lessons and removes lessons that no longer apply. The lesson changes are part of the pull request, so the review sees them.
options.change: Keep export const lessons = "file" as LessonsMode in develop/lessons.ts. preparePull in develop/pull.ts then sends the GitHub prepare payload {"lessons": true}, keeps the returned text and size in the task, and develop/report.ts gives them to each turn of develop/turn.ts.

options.label: No lessons
options.summary: No turn reads or writes the lessons file.
options.change: In develop/lessons.ts set export const lessons = "none" as LessonsMode. preparePull then sends the GitHub prepare payload {} and the turn prompts do not name the lessons file.
